title: XVI: A Forest Walk

teacherSummary.text: Hester waits in the forest for Dimmesdale. Sunlight flickers around Pearl but flees from Hester. Pearl asks about the Black Man; Hester says she met him once, and the letter is his mark. The brook babbles but tells no secrets.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Mother … the sunshine does not love you” slowly and put it in my own words: In the forest, Pearl says the sunlight runs from her mother because of something on her breast. Next, craft. I notice the childlike personification of sunshine as a creature that loves or avoids people. The strongest word is “sunshine”: it stands for joy and grace, which seem to flee the letter. Then, effect. What is Pearl suggesting when she says the sunshine does not love Hester? My answer: Pearl voices what the town believes, that the letter cuts Hester off from happiness; the moment prepares for Hester throwing the letter off and the sun pouring in.
